title: Nexova Telemetry Event Catalogue
description: Normative schema catalogue for the Nexova telemetry plan. `envelope` is the draft-07 schema every emitted event must satisfy. Each entry in `events` carries a `properties_schema` (draft-07) that the event's `properties` object must satisfy; `additionalProperties: false` inside it enforces the property allowlist. `definitions.eventEntry` documents the catalogue entry shape. Hypotheses, decisions, instrumentation points, and delivery rationale live in telemetry-plan.md; hypothesis/decision wording here is identical to that document, where the strings complete the sentence "We capture event_type because {hypothesis}, which allows us to make the decision to {decision}" with the first letter's case adapted to sentence position and the hypothesis's trailing period yielded to the sentence comma.

envelope.description: The standard Event Envelope: mandatory fields present on every event emitted by any source.

eventId.description: UUIDv4 unique per event instance. Generated by the emitter: crypto.randomUUID() on the web, uuid.uuid4() on the APIs.

timestamp.description: Emission time in ISO 8601 UTC with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-10-19T00:32:22.000Z. Always emitter-UTC; no local offsets.

sessionId.description: UUIDv4 identifying one browser page-lifetime session. The web client keeps it in session memory (no sessionStorage), rotates it on successful login, rotates back to anonymous on logout/401, and sends it as the X-Session-Id header. A hard reload starts a new anonymous session and re-binds to a valid token. The APIs adopt the header when present and generate a fresh per-request UUID otherwise (server-side session, not persisted). Never null.

userId.description: Stringified TinyDB user id (integer) from the JWT `sub` claim. NOT the user_uuid stored on orders; join via the admin /users lookup. Null when the request is unauthenticated. Never an email and never the uuid.

event_type.description: Event identifier in entity_action taxonomy with past-tense verbs. Must be one of the keys of the `events` map.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS event's properties_schema, matching the event's `schema_version` field in the catalogue.

requestId.description: Correlation id. The web client generates one UUIDv4 per user action/fetch and sends it as X-Request-Id; API middleware adopts the header (or generates one) and echoes it in the X-Request-Id response header. All events caused by one user action — frontend and backend — share one requestId.

source.description: Emitter discriminator used for routing in the capture pipeline.

properties.description: Flat, event-specific payload. Always present (`{}` allowed). The allowlist is enforced by the per-event `properties_schema` (additionalProperties: false), which `properties` MUST also be validated against.

inbound_order_created.description: A new batch of training or onboarding material arrives from a supplier (AssetEntry persisted).
inbound_order_created.hypothesis: We need to know how much material is being produced/purchased, for which programme, and at what cost.
inbound_order_created.decision: Plan material production based on expected enrolment demand (Elena).

office.description: Office where the inbound order was registered (lowercase per the Nexova briefing).

product_id.description: Asset id (Product) the order adds stock to.

product_category.description: Category of the product per the Nexova briefing taxonomy.

programme_id.description: Programme slug the material belongs to, e.g. b2b-sales, basic-leadership.

currency.description: Local currency of the office (EUR Valencia, USD Miami). Never converted at the telemetry layer.

supplier.description: Supplier company name (business data, not a person).

unit_cost.description: Unit cost of this order in the office currency. Required by EC5 (unit_cost/currency fields) before this event can fire.

order_id.description: AssetEntry.id of the persisted inbound order.

pii.sanitisation: None required. Supplier is a company name; the acting user is the envelope userId (stringified internal id). No candidate, client, or consultant names are ever captured.

outbound_order_created.description: A kit or certificate is delivered to a client, candidate, consultant, or agent (AssetExit persisted).
outbound_order_created.hypothesis: We need to know which programmes consume the most material, and at what rate.
outbound_order_created.decision: Anticipate restocking needs before a large enrolment wave (Elena).

office.description: Office where the outbound order was registered (lowercase).

product_id.description: Asset id (Product) the order removes stock from.

product_category.description: Category of the product per the Nexova briefing taxonomy.

programme_id.description: Programme slug the material belongs to, e.g. b2b-sales, basic-leadership.

quantity.description: Units delivered or consumed in this order.

currency.description: Local currency of the office (EUR Valencia, USD Miami). Never converted at the telemetry layer.

exit_type.description: Allocation (to a person) or consumption (training use). The only allocation signal captured.

order_id.description: AssetExit.id of the persisted outbound order.

pii.sanitisation: The `assigned_to` recipient name is NEVER captured — not even as a presence flag. The Nexova briefing forbids candidate, client, and consultant names in properties; `exit_type` is the only allocation signal.

stock_threshold_triggered.description: The stock of a material item falls below the configured minimum. Edge-triggered: fires only on the crossing (previous_stock >= min_stock > new_stock).
stock_threshold_triggered.hypothesis: We need to know how often a programme runs out of available material.
stock_threshold_triggered.decision: Adjust the minimum threshold or speed up reprinting/reproduction of that material.
stock_threshold_triggered.throttle: Edge-triggered: emit only when stock crosses from at-or-above min_stock to below it, checked after each outbound commit. Additionally capped at 1 event per product_id per 60 minutes.

product_id.description: Asset id (Product) whose stock crossed the threshold.

product_category.description: Category of the product per the Nexova briefing taxonomy.

programme_id.description: Programme slug the material belongs to.

quantity.description: Current stock after the order that caused the crossing (can be 0).

currency.description: Local currency of the office. Never converted at the telemetry layer.

min_stock.description: The configured minimum threshold for this product.

previous_stock.description: Stock immediately before the order that caused the crossing.

pii.sanitisation: None required. Purely business data.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.description: A user attempts to modify stock directly (outside an order) and the system rejects the attempt.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.hypothesis: We need to know if staff are attempting to bypass material traceability controls.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.decision: Reinforce training or permissions at the office where this happens most (Patricia).

office.description: Office of the targeted product; null when the product id could not be resolved.

product_id.description: Targeted asset id parsed from the path when numeric; null otherwise.

product_category.description: Category of the targeted product; null when it could not be resolved.

programme_id.description: Programme slug of the targeted product; null when it could not be resolved.

quantity.description: Always null: no stock movement occurs on rejection. Key retained so every mandatory inventory event carries the briefing's minimum property set.

currency.description: Local currency of the resolved office; null when the office is unknown.

method.description: HTTP method of the rejected attempt.

path.description: Route template of the rejected attempt, e.g. /inventory/products/{id}. Never the raw URL with real ids.

pii.sanitisation: None required. The acting user is the envelope userId; no payload content is captured.

kit_cost_variance_detected.description: The unit cost of an inbound order varies more than 10% from the historical value for that material/supplier pair.
kit_cost_variance_detected.hypothesis: We need to know when a material supplier raises prices abnormally.
kit_cost_variance_detected.decision: Alert Elena and Laura to renegotiate or find an alternate supplier.
kit_cost_variance_detected.throttle: Capped at 1 event per (product_id, supplier) per 24 hours to suppress alert storms on multi-line orders.

office.description: Office where the inbound order was registered.

product_id.description: Asset id (Product) of the ordered material.

product_category.description: Category of the product per the Nexova briefing taxonomy.

programme_id.description: Programme slug the material belongs to.

quantity.description: Units in the inbound order that triggered the detection.

currency.description: Local currency of the office. Never converted at the telemetry layer.

supplier.description: Supplier company name whose price varied.

unit_cost.description: Unit cost of the new order.

historical_avg_cost.description: Historical mean unit cost for this (product, supplier) pair.

variance_percent.description: Signed variance, e.g. 15.0 means +15% over the historical mean.

order_id.description: AssetEntry.id of the inbound order that triggered the detection.

pii.sanitisation: None required. Supplier is a company name; no personal data is captured.

product_created.description: A new material item (Product/Asset) is added to the catalogue.
product_created.hypothesis: We need to know how the catalogue grows per office and per programme, which reveals where material types are proliferating.
product_created.decision: Identify unplanned item proliferation and standardise catalogues (Patricia/Elena).

office.description: Office that owns the new product.

product_id.description: Asset id (Product) of the created product.

product_category.description: Category of the product per the Nexova briefing taxonomy.

programme_id.description: Programme slug the new product belongs to.

quantity.description: Always 0: a freshly created asset starts at zero stock.

currency.description: Local currency of the office. Never converted at the telemetry layer.

sku.description: Structured SKU of the new product. The free-text product name is excluded.

min_stock.description: Configured minimum-stock threshold for the new product.

pii.sanitisation: The product free-text `name` is excluded (it could embed personal names); only the structured `sku` and ids are captured.

outbound_order_rejected.description: An outbound order is rejected by the API because the requested quantity exceeds available stock.
outbound_order_rejected.hypothesis: We need to know when deliveries are rejected for lack of stock, per programme.
outbound_order_rejected.decision: Trigger earlier restocking and validate demand forecasts (Elena).

programme_id.description: Programme slug of the targeted product.

currency.description: Local currency of the office. Never converted at the telemetry layer.

exit_type.description: Exit type of the rejected order.

available_stock.description: Stock available at the moment of rejection.

pii.sanitisation: None required. The `assigned_to` value is never captured, consistent with the briefing's names ban.

supplier_rate_edited.description: An admin or manager changes a supplier's monthly rate.
supplier_rate_edited.hypothesis: We need to know how often each supplier's rate changes and in which direction.
supplier_rate_edited.decision: Feed supplier negotiation and cost-variance investigations (Laura).

supplier_id.description: TinyDB doc id of the supplier whose rate changed.

currency.description: Currency of the supplier record. Never converted at the telemetry layer.

pii.sanitisation: Supplier `contact_email` and `notes` are never captured; the acting user is the envelope userId.

incident_report_analyzed.description: The incident analyzer processes an uploaded CSV and produces metrics.
incident_report_analyzed.hypothesis: We need to know how much the incident analyzer is used and how heavy its workloads are.
incident_report_analyzed.decision: Plan analyzer capacity and track adoption of Roberto's support line.

row_count.description: Total rows in the analyzed CSV (metrics['total']).

duration_ms.description: Processing time of the analysis in milliseconds.

pii.sanitisation: Only aggregate counts are captured. CSV contents (which may contain personal data) are never captured. The endpoint is unauthenticated, so envelope.userId is null — documented as a known limitation.

login_succeeded.description: A user authenticates successfully and receives a JWT.
login_succeeded.hypothesis: We need to know account usage patterns: who logs in, when, and how often.
login_succeeded.decision: Identify inactive accounts for cleanup and spot unusual login-time clustering (Laura/Patricia).

pii.sanitisation: Empty allowlist by design. The email is omitted entirely; identity lives in the envelope userId (internal id).

login_failed.description: A login attempt is rejected (unknown email, wrong password, inactive account, or corrupt hash).
login_failed.hypothesis: We need to know whether login failures are forgotten credentials or attack patterns.
login_failed.decision: Detect credential attacks and target security training (Patricia).
login_failed.throttle: Capped at 60 events per minute per service to bound brute-force storms while preserving the spike shape.

pii.sanitisation: The attempted email is NEVER captured, not even hashed — the staff is small enough that hashes would be trivially re-identifiable. For unknown_email the envelope userId is null; otherwise the resolved internal id is used.

session_expired.description: A JWT is found to be expired — either by the API during a request or by the client-side AuthGuard.
session_expired.hypothesis: We need to know how often sessions expire mid-use and where that friction happens.
session_expired.decision: Tune token_expiry_minutes and improve the session UX.

detected_by.description: client = AuthGuard expiry check; server = API token decode (requires EC2 to distinguish expiry from invalid signature).

pii.sanitisation: No credential content is captured; only the detection channel.

password_reset_requested.description: A user requests a password reset through the forgot-password flow.
password_reset_requested.hypothesis: We need to know how much password-recovery demand exists over time.
password_reset_requested.decision: Target onboarding improvements and evaluate SSO (Patricia).

pii.sanitisation: Empty allowlist by design. The email is omitted entirely; the endpoint already anti-enumerates registered addresses and telemetry must not weaken that.

password_reset_failed.description: A password-reset flow fails (email service unavailable, or an invalid/used/expired reset token).
password_reset_failed.hypothesis: We need to know which failure mode dominates the reset flow.
password_reset_failed.decision: Fix email-configuration issues proactively and measure reset-token abuse.

reason.description: Failure mode: 503 email-configuration/delivery branches, or the invalid-token branches of reset-password.

pii.sanitisation: Emails and reset tokens are never captured.

user_registered.description: A new account is created through the registration endpoint.
user_registered.hypothesis: We need to know the account-creation rate as a leading indicator of staff onboarding volume.
user_registered.decision: Forecast onboarding-kit demand (Patricia, including Roberto's 30 outsourced support agents).

pii.sanitisation: The registered email is never captured. Note: the User model has no office field, so office correlation for registrations is impossible today — documented as future work.

admin_role_changed.description: An admin changes another user's role.
admin_role_changed.hypothesis: We need to know how often privileges change, in which direction, and by whom.

target_user_id.description: TinyDB user id of the user whose role changed (the acting admin is the envelope userId).

pii.sanitisation: Internal ids and roles only; no emails or names.

page_view.description: An operator navigates to a backoffice route.
page_view.hypothesis: We need to know which backoffice sections operators actually visit most.
page_view.decision: Prioritise features and training on hot sections; simplify or cut underused ones.
page_view.throttle: No dropping (visit counts are the point); transport-level batching only: flush no later than 10 s after the first pending event or at 20 events, then use navigator.sendBeacon on visibilitychange to hidden with a normal-send fallback when Beacon is refused.

page_path.description: Route path with the query string ALWAYS stripped — /login?next=... and /reset-password?token=... must never leak.

load_duration_ms.description: Optional. Navigation duration from performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0].duration on first route mount.

referrer_path.description: Optional. Same-origin referring path (query stripped); never a cross-origin URL.

pii.sanitisation: Query strings are stripped from page_path and referrer_path, which removes ?token= and ?next= leaks. No form contents or user input are captured.

form_abandoned.description: An operator leaves a form after entering data but without submitting it successfully.
form_abandoned.hypothesis: We need to know which flows lose operators before completion.
form_abandoned.decision: Redesign or re-train on the abandoned flows.
form_abandoned.throttle: Natural: 1 event per (sessionId, flow_id) at unmount time.

page_path.description: Route path of the form page (query string stripped).

pii.sanitisation: NO field values are ever captured — not asset ids, quantities, names, or emails. Only the flow id and the page path.

api_latency_recorded.description: An API request takes 500 ms or longer to complete.
api_latency_recorded.hypothesis: We need to know which endpoints are slow and when slowness spikes.
api_latency_recorded.decision: Fix or optimise the slow endpoints operators depend on (ops team).
api_latency_recorded.throttle: Emit only when duration >= 500 ms; debounce 1 event per (service, method, path) per 60 seconds. Sub-threshold requests emit nothing (counter-only).

path.description: Route template (request.scope['route'].path) when resolvable; otherwise the raw path with numeric segments replaced by {id}. Never high-cardinality raw paths.

status_code.description: HTTP status code of the response.

pii.sanitisation: No query strings, bodies, or headers are captured; only the route template and status.

frontend_error_captured.description: An uncaught error or unhandled promise rejection occurs in the backoffice web app.
frontend_error_captured.hypothesis: We need to know which pages crash or throw in production.
frontend_error_captured.decision: Fix the top-crash pages first (dev team).
frontend_error_captured.throttle: Cap 10 events per minute per session; identical (error_type, message) suppressed for 5 minutes.

message.description: Sanitised error message: truncated to 300 chars with emails and URLs stripped by regex.

page_path.description: Route path where the error occurred (query string stripped).

stack_frame.description: Optional. First stack frame only, in 'file:line' form; the full stack is never captured.

pii.sanitisation: Error messages may contain emails, URLs, or user content. The emitter strips emails/URLs by regex and truncates to 300 chars; only the first stack frame is captured; page_path has its query string stripped.

network_request_failed.description: A browser fetch to one of the APIs fails at the network level (service down, unreachable).
network_request_failed.hypothesis: We need to know which APIs fail from operators' browsers.
network_request_failed.decision: Prioritise service fixes and monitor availability (ops team).
network_request_failed.throttle: Debounce 1 event per (target, page_path) per 60 seconds.

target.description: Normalised 'service:path' of the failed call, e.g. inventory-api:/inventory/orders/inbound, query string stripped.

page_path.description: Route path the operator was on (query string stripped).

pii.sanitisation: No request bodies or headers are captured; only the normalised target and page path.

validation_failed.description: A form submission or API request is rejected by validation (client-side rules or a server 422).
validation_failed.hypothesis: We need to know which forms and endpoints generate the most invalid submissions.
validation_failed.decision: Redesign the offending forms or clarify field rules (ops/UX).
validation_failed.throttle: Client: 1 per (context, reason) per 60 s per session. Server: cap 10 per minute per endpoint.

source.description: client = web form validation; server = API 422 handler.

context.description: Form id (e.g. inbound_order_form) or endpoint path template (e.g. /inventory/orders/inbound).

field.description: Field name only — NEVER the submitted value.

reason.description: Rule code, e.g. quantity_gt_0, assigned_to_required, asset_required.

page_path.description: Optional. Route path, client events only (query string stripped).

pii.sanitisation: Submitted values are NEVER captured — only field names and rule codes. This makes the event PII-free by construction.
